## Hepatocellular Carcinoma

::::: columns
::: {.column width="35%"}
-   Liver cancer ranks as the [6th]{.alert} most common cancer and
    [3rd]{.alert} leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide

-   Hepatocellular carcinoma represents [75-85%]{.alert} of all liver
    cancer cases wordwide.

-   5-year survival rates in the U.S. have risen from 3% (1975-1977) to
    22% (2014-2020)
:::

::: {.column width="65%"}
![Worldwide Epidemiology of Liver Cancer in
2018](images/liver-cancer-epidemiology.jpg)
:::
:::::

## Where Y90 Fits Diagnosis

::::: columns
::: {.column width="40%"}
Y90 is suited for liver-dominant disease, especially:

-   BCLC A tumors not amenable to ablation

-   BCLC B intermediate tumors

-   Select BCLC C patients with portal vein thrombosis
:::

::: {.column width="60%"}
![](images/TARE-image.png){.lightbox}
:::
:::::

# Historical Evolution of Y90

## 1960s - 1990s

:::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
-   In 1951, Bierman et al demonstrated angiographically that liver
    tumors received their blood supply from the hepatic artery and not
    the portal vein.

-   1967, Ariel & Pack perform first Y90 administration in four patients
:::

:::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {layout="[1, 1, 1]"}
![](images/ariel-and-pack-1967/fig1.png){.lightbox height="200"}

![](images/ariel-and-pack-1967/fig2.png){.lightbox height="200"}

![](images/ariel-and-pack-1967/fig3.png){.lightbox height="200"}
:::
::::
::::::

## 2000s - Present

::::: columns
::: {.column width="40%"}
1999: TheraSphere granted a humanitarian device exemption for use in
patients with unresectable HCC.

2016: SIR-Spheres approved for the treatment of unresectable metastatic
liver tumors from primary colorectal cancer with adjuvant intrahepatic
artery chemotherapy.

2025: SIR-Spheres for the treatment of unresectable hepatocellular
carcinoma (HCC) following the [DOORwaY-90]{.alert} study
:::

::: {.column width="60%" layout="[1,1]"}
![](images/y90/sir-sphere.png){width="259"}

![](images/y90/thera-spheres.jpg){width="300"}
:::
:::::

# Establishing TARE in the HCC Algorithm

## SARAH Trial

:::::: columns
::: {.column width="40%"}
-   Phase III, open-label, randomized controlled trial

-   $^{90}$Y Resin Microspheres vs. Sorafenib for advanced HCC (BCLC C)

-   [No significant difference in overall survival]{.alert} (8.0 months
    for Y90 vs. 9.9 months for sorafenib)

-   Radioembolization associated with [fewer adverse events]{.alert} and
    better quality of life
:::

::: {.column width="30%"}
![](images/sarah-trial-1.gif){.lightbox}
:::

::: {.column width="30%"}
![](images/sarah-trial-2.png){.lightbox}
:::
::::::

## SIRveNIB Trial

:::::: columns
::: {.column width="40%"}
-   Phase III, open-label, randomized controlled trial

-   $^{90}$Y Resin Microspheres vs. Sorafenib for advanced HCC (BCLC B
    or C) in the Asia-Pacific

-   [No significant difference in overall survival]{.alert} (8.8 months
    for Y90 vs. 10.0 months for sorafenib)

-   Radioembolization showed significantly [fewer grade 3 adverse fewer
    adverse events]{.alert} (27.7% vs. 50.6%)
:::

::: {.column width="30%"}
![](images/sirvenib-trial-1.jpg){.lightbox}
:::

::: {.column width="30%"}
![](images/sirvenib-trial-2.jpg){.lightbox}
:::
::::::

## DOSISPHERE-01 Trial

:::::: columns
::: {.column width="40%"}
-   Phase III, open-label, randomized controlled trial

-   Personalized Dosimetry (≥205 Gy target) vs. Standard Dosimetry (∼120
    Gy target)

-   Personalized dosimetry showed [higher median overall
    survival]{.alert} (26.6 months for vs. 10.7 months)

-   Also showed [higher tumor responses response rates]{.alert} (71% vs.
    36%) and [increased rates of downstaging]{.alert} to surgical
    treatments (35% vs. 3.5%)\
:::

::: {.column width="30%"}
![](images/dosisphere-trial-1.gif){.lightbox}
:::

::: {.column width="30%"}
![](images/dosisphere-trial-2.jpg){.lightbox}
:::
::::::

## TRACE Trial

:::::: columns
::: {.column width="40%"}
-   Y90 Radioembolization vs. Drug-Eluting Bead Chemoembolization
    (DEB-TACE)

-   The trial was stopped early because the primary endpoint (TTP) was
    met in favor of Y90

-   Y90 TARE showed [superior median overall]{.alert} (30.2 months vs.
    15.6 months)
:::

::: {.column width="30%"}
![](images/premiere-trial-2.jpg){.lightbox}
:::

::: {.column width="30%"}
![](images/premiere-trial-1.jpg){.lightbox}
:::
::::::

# Modern Y90 Concepts

## Radiation Segmentectomy

::::: columns
::: {.column width="60%"}
Superselective infusion of a very high dose (\> 400 Gy)

Evidence:

-   LEGACY trial: ORR 90%, median OS \~45 months

Pearls:

-   Identify variant anatomy (parasitizing supply, accessory/replaced
    vessels)
-   Different segments are associated with different post-embolization
    complications
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}
![](images/toon-y90-segmentectomy.jpeg){.lightbox .nostretch
width="256"}
:::
:::::

## Radiation Lobectomy

::::: columns
::: {.column width="60%"}
Lobar dose to induce hypertrophy of the contralateral lobe

Alternative to portal vein embolization

Provides tumor control while waiting for future liver remnant (FLR)
growth
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}
![](images/toon-y90-lobectomy.jpeg){.lightbox width="249"}
:::
:::::

## Personalized Dosimetry

::::: columns
::: column
Old model: everyone gets the same dose

Modern model

-   99mTc-MAA SPECT/CT

-   Voxel- or partition-based dosimetry

-   Targeted dose delivery

Evidence

-   DOSISPHERE-01: OS 10.7 → 26.6 mo
:::

::: column
![](images/dosimetry.jpg){.lightbox width="496"}
:::
:::::

## Patient Selection

::::: columns

::: {.column width="40%"}
-   Child-Pugh A and early B

-   Liver-dominant disease

-   Assess vascular anatomy and shunting

-   Multidisciplinary input with hepatology and surgery
:::

::: {.column width="60%"}
![](images/bclc-2025.jpg){.lightbox}
:::

:::::

## Mapping Angiogram

Comprehensive vascular mapping with CBCT to identify tumor supply and
prevent extrahepatic deposition.

::::: columns

::: {.column width="40%"}
-   Selective catherization

-   Identify variant hepatic arterial anatomy

-   Coil embolization of gastroduodenal or right gastric artery

-   MAA injection to estimate lung shunt and dosimetry
:::

::: {.column width="60%"}
![MAA SPECT/CT
Scan](https://media.springernature.com/lw1200/springer-static/image/art%3A10.1186%2Fs13550-018-0402-8/MediaObjects/13550_2018_402_Fig6_HTML.png){.lightbox}
:::

:::::

## Treatment Day

::::: columns

::: {.column width="40%"}
-   Selective catheterization

-   Deliver microspheres slowly under fluoroscopy

-   Post-treatment SPECT or PET imaging
:::

::: {.column width="60%"}
![](images/tare-and-followup.jpg){.lightbox}
:::
